title: L1b(ii) CLOSED AT THE DERIVATION LEVEL (negative): the binding Type-I step of the Conrey/PRZZ extraction has only ONE exploitable variable at the phase level; the apparent (a, f1) two-variable form is the ADDITIVE-bilinear sum Sigma_a nu(a) Sigma_{f1} mu~(f1) e_v(f1 x_a), whose known optimal treatment at this regime IS the paper's W'-splitting + per-block Weil (the published TI1 term). The 2026 bilinear Kloosterman estimates cannot be applied to it. Both L1b sub-lanes (0432 = literature, 0435 = derivation) now close: the 4/7 wall has no known input.
facts: SETUP (from 0428/0430, image-verbatim core re-read today from the section 3.2.5 Type I derivation): after the binomial separation and summation by parts, the Type I sum reduces to Sigma_{a<=A} nu(a) Sigma_{v~=V} r(v) Sigma_{e~=E,(e,dv)=1} beta(e) Sigma_{f~=F} (log f)^l FdU^2(def) mu(f) e(-a n(v,e,d)/v), and by inclusion-exclusion mu(f) the f-sum factorizes over h^2 with the inner sum over f1: Sigma_{f1 in I/h, (f1,dev)=1} (weighted) e_v(f1 x) - a ONE-VARIABLE additive-character (completed Kloosterman, degenerate S_c(m,0)-type) sum with trivial bound F'/h^2 and Weil bound T^eps v^{1/2}(n,v)(1+F'v^{-1}), combined by min(x,y) <= (xy)^{1/2} - exactly the step audited in 0430.

THE (ii) QUESTION (from 0430): is there a RE-DECOMPOSITION in which the Kloosterman step is genuinely two-variable with both axes of length ~ c^{1/2}? Answer: NO, for the following derivation-level reasons: (a) before inclusion-exclusion the phase e(-a n(v,e,d)/v) depends on a but NOT on f - f enters the phase only as a WEIGHT (mu(f) (log f)^l FdU^2(def)); (b) the only (a, f1) bilinear form that exists, Sigma_a nu(a) Sigma_{f1} mu~(f1) e_v(f1 x_a) (x_a = x(n(a),v)), is ADDITIVE-bilinear - a linear-in-f1 character with a-dependent argument, i.e. the completed degeneracy S_v(f1 x_a, 0), NOT a non-degenerate Kloosterman S_v(m a, n b); (c) the known optimal treatment of exactly this additive-bilinear form at the critical regime IS the paper's W' = U^{1/4} block splitting + Weil-per-block (the a-range gets consumed by the block structure; the resulting TI1 = T^{5/8 + 5 theta/8} is the optimized output); (d) the 2026 bilinear-Kloosterman estimates (BP 2607.24311, Pascadi non-abelian amplification, Milicevic-Qin-Wu 2511.07550, Kerr-Shparlinski-Wu 2204.05038 - all audited in 0430/0432) require the non-degenerate two-argument Kloosterman phase S_c(m a, n b) with both ranges ~ c^{1/2}; they cannot be applied to the degenerate additive form (b), and no published power-saving estimate for the mu~-twisted additive-bilinear form at critical length exists (0432: the short-sum/weighted literature is short-regime and prime-modulus only).

VERDICT: L1b(ii) closes at the derivation level - exactly as L1b(i) closed at the literature level (0432). The 4/7 wall (LevWall7 double-waste + LevWall8 machine legs, 0430) has no known published input; the two live structural openings for future work are both research-grade open problems: (i') a new power-saving estimate for the mu~-twisted ONE-variable incomplete Kloosterman/additive sum at critical length and general composite modulus (would be a standalone major result); (ii') a genuinely new DECOMPOSITION of the mollifier error term that produces a non-degenerate two-argument Kloosterman phase at the binding step (the a-axis in the current extraction is structurally bounded by the hDelta bookkeeping A = N1 N2/(d^2 T^{1-eps}) <= T^eps - a different decomposition would need to start before the hDelta completion, i.e. a different mollifier treatment). Both are recorded, neither is claimed feasible.

By Weil's bound for Kloosterman sums [26] ... Taking the minimum of these two bounds and using min(x,y) <= (xy)^{1/2}', the post-sum bound '(1+|w|) T^eps A(W^{1/2} U^{1/2} V^{5/4} + U V^{3/4})', and the Conrey sentence about applying Weil directly).
